column3: The Hebrew explicitly says “over His people, over Israel” and names “the voice of the words of the LORD”; BSB condenses both expressions.
The Hebrew uses the names Amalek and Israel in the singular and explicitly names the action as setting against Israel on the way; BSB uses plural people names.
The Hebrew changes to plural “you shall devote” within otherwise singular commands and uses singular collective names and individual animals; BSB uses plurals throughout.
The Hebrew calls them “the people”; BSB calls them troops.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul and uses collective singular “the Kenite”, then switches between plural commands and singular address; BSB uses plural Kenites throughout.
The Hebrew has the singular name Amalek and says Shur is “before Egypt”; BSB gives the people and specifies east of Egypt.
The Hebrew calls those destroyed “all the people” and retains the mouth of the sword; BSB says “all the others” and “with the sword”.
The Hebrew calls those with Saul “the people”; BSB calls them troops.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew retains the image of setting up his words and uses a burning expression for Samuel’s reaction; BSB has carrying out instructions and being distressed.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Samuel’s name and says he rose to meet Saul, without expressly naming a confrontation.
The Hebrew repeats Saul’s name as Samuel’s destination and describes the LORD’s word, singular, as set up; BSB has a pronoun and “instructions”.
The Hebrew calls the two animal sounds voices and explicitly names Samuel’s ears; BSB has bleating and lowing without the ears.
The Hebrew first uses unnamed “they brought” and then names “the people”; BSB makes troops the explicit subject of bringing.
The Hebrew explicitly names Samuel and Saul in the first exchange, then leaves the replying speaker unnamed; BSB names Saul in that reply.
The Hebrew has no explicit “once” or verb “become” in the smallness and headship clauses.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name, calls the mission a way, and names Amalek in the singular.
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD’s voice and eyes; BSB leaves the voice implicit and has “in the sight”.
The Hebrew explicitly names Samuel as Saul’s audience, repeats the LORD’s voice, and calls Amalek a singular name.
The Hebrew calls the group the people, not troops.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name before the voice; BSB uses “His voice”.
The Hebrew names teraphim and uses direct equations rather than explicit comparison words “like”.
The Hebrew retains the LORD’s mouth and calls Samuel’s instructions his words.
The Hebrew uses the image of lifting his sin and describes worship as bowing down.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul as Samuel’s audience and repeats the LORD’s name; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew leaves the person grabbing unnamed; BSB explicitly names Saul.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the verb for regretting; BSB uses “change His mind”.
The Hebrew does not repeat Saul’s name as speaker; BSB names him.
